parcel.property_class: Dwelling (lot 002); Single Struct on Multi Lot (lot 002A)
parcel.note: One structure spanning two contiguous lots. Lot 002A is classed 'Single Struct on Multi Lot' and reports 0 building area — the building is carried on lot 002. Both parcels' assessor property_location reads 129 24th Avenue. Building measurements are from lot 002.

assessment.note: No sale recorded on the current roll for either parcel.

historic_status.reason: Lot 002: Historic Survey Result and 45 years or older. Lot 002A: no evaluation and 45 years or older

notable_residents.name: Ansel Adams
notable_residents.detail: The source records 129 as Adams's childhood home, giving his birth on 20 February 1902, and 131 as a later property with a studio that it says was destroyed in a sinkhole. The city treats the two numbers as one structure on two lots, so this page documents them together; the guide's split between the two numbers is carried as its own account.

permit_summary.note: DBI files the shared foundation permits under both lot 002 and lot 002A, so the raw query returns each twice; duplicates are collapsed here. The 1995–96 run is repeated underpinning and stem-wall foundation work along the north side of the building.

permits.description: revision to permit 202407166594 — add an elevator and equipment room at the existing laundry room and crawlspace
lower level: remove stairs, add a new stair up to the main level; remodel the sunroom, kitchen and bathroom; remodel upper-level bedrooms
emergency repair of the deck over the garage — replace structural beams and guardrails, waterproofing and deck surface
build a 7-foot fence along the north property line and remove an existing shed
renewal of the 1998 addition permits for final sign-off
construct a stem-wall foundation along the north side of the dwelling
underpin the building to provide stability to the house (lot 002 / 129)
emergency underpinning of two corners of the house

sections.heading: One building, two lots and two numbers
sections.body: The city treats 129 and 131 as a single structure on two parcels. The 131 lot is classed “Single Struct on Multi Lot” and reports zero building area — the building is carried entirely on the 129 lot — and both parcels' assessor records give the location as 129 24th Avenue. This site documents them as one building, which is why the page is titled with the range.

sections.heading: The guide's account
sections.body: A published guide records 129 as Ansel Adams's childhood home, giving his birth on 20 February 1902, and 131 as a later property with a studio it says was destroyed in a sinkhole. The city data does not separate the two numbers into two buildings, so the guide's account of two houses is set out here rather than adopted.
